newsitem.title: USA: Fla. anti-tobacco lawyer can seek punitive damages.
newsitem.headline: Fla. anti-tobacco lawyer can seek punitive damages.

text.p: A Florida judge has ruled that an attorney suing R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co on behalf of an ailing smoker can ask a jury to award punitive damages.

In a ruling issued Thursday, Circuit Judge Michael Weatherby said attorney Norwood "Woody" Wilner, who last year won a $750,000 damage award on behalf of a smoker, can ask the jury to punish Reynolds when the product liability lawsuit of JoAnn Karbiwnyk goes to trial October 6.

Wilner, who has not decided how much money to ask for, argued at a hearing earlier this month that Reynolds deserved to be punished for hiding research about the dangers of smoking and doing nothing to make cigarettes safer.
Reynolds' attorneys argued that the company is a leader in research to make cigarettes safer.

In May, Wilner asked a jury to award punitive damages in a wrongful death lawsuit filed by the family of Jean Connor, a heavy smoker who died of lung cancer. But the jury decided that Reynolds was not responsible for Connor's death and no damages were awarded.
Last year, Wilner persuaded a jury to award $750,000 in compensatory damages to smoker Grady Carter, who claimed his cancer was caused by cigarettes. He did not seek punitive damages in that case.

Karbiwnyk, 58, of Orange Park, Florida, has lung cancer that spread to her brain. She started smoking in the mid-1950s and eventually switched to Reynolds' Winston and Salem brand cigarettes, smoking as much as one-and-a-half packs, or 30 cigarettes, a day until 1984, when she quit.
Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
